tags: Gilgamesh and Enkidu and the Netherworld
description: Explores five independent Sumerian Bilgames compositions: Gilgamesh and Aga, Gilgamesh and Huwawa, Gilgamesh and Enkidu and the Netherworld, the Bull of Heaven, and the Death of Gilgamesh. Compares political counsel, the pursuit of fame, obligations to the dead and the changing role of Enkidu with the later Akkadian epic, explaining what divergent and fragmentary manuscripts allow readers to reconstruct.

setting.label: c. 2700 BCE · legendary Uruk frame
setting.note: The 001000 manuscript and its historical-setting companion explicitly place the traditional king around 2700 BCE, while denying a securely established contemporary biography. This is a legendary narrative frame, not a date for the monsters, flood, composition, or surviving tablets. Metropolitan Museum of Art: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/gilgamesh

witness.label: Early 2nd millennium BCE · surviving Sumerian copies
witness.note: 008000 explains that many surviving Sumerian literary witnesses date to the early second millennium BCE, not to the age of the legendary king or the initial creation of each tale. Numeric bounds deliberately retain whole-millennium precision.
